here-there-and-everywhere: Lord Frederic Hamilton, a British diplomat, soldier, and member of Parliament, fills this memoir with stories from a life spent across the empire. From African campaigns to London drawing rooms, he recalls the people and odd incidents he met along the way. Told with dry wit and no great reverence for rank, it is an insider's tour of the late Victorian world.
history-of-american-literature: Reuben Post Halleck's survey takes students from colonial beginnings through the flowering of American letters. Irving, Hawthorne, Emerson, Whitman, and Twain each receive their chapter in a narrative of how a new nation found its voice. Long used in American classrooms, the book offers a solid, readable map of the country's literary past.
nan-sherwood-at-rose-ranch-or-the-old-me: Annie Roe Carr sends her plucky heroine Nan Sherwood west to Rose Ranch, where an old Mexican's hidden treasure sets off a lively hunt. Nan and her friends ride, explore, and outwit the villains with the resourcefulness series readers loved. A cheerful girls' adventure in the classic Stratemeyer-era mold.
castle-nowhere: Constance Fenimore Woolson sets this novel among the islands and shores of the Great Lakes, a region she knew intimately. Her characters — dreamers and wanderers drawn to the water — live out quiet dramas of love and loss against the vast inland seas. Woolson, a friend of Henry James, wrote with a subtlety that has won her lasting admirers.
elsie-dinsmore: Martha Finley's 1867 novel introduced Elsie Dinsmore, the pious little heroine who became one of children's literature's most famous characters. Orphaned Elsie clings to her faith and her Bible through trials with a stern father and a tempting world. Millions of young readers wept over her story, making it a landmark of Victorian moral fiction for girls.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: Every region has its buried treasure, and Skinner devotes this volume to America's lost gold, pirate hoards, and miser caches. From Captain Kidd's fabled loot to frontier strongboxes, the tales blend history with hopeful dreaming. Readers will enjoy the legends — though Skinner makes no promises about the digging.
sidonia-the-sorceress-the-supposed-destr: Wilhelm Meinhold's eerie German novel — translated by Lady Wilde, Oscar's mother — tells of Sidonia von Bork, accused of witchcraft against the dukes of Pomerania. Trial records and dark legend blend into a gothic tale of magic, malice, and doom. A strange, powerful classic of supernatural fiction.
the-press-gang-afloat-and-ashore: J. R. Hutchinson tells the rough story of the press-gang — the naval press that seized men for Britain's wars afloat and ashore. Riots, escapes, and the harsh life of impressed sailors fill a vivid historical account. A revealing look at the dark side of the age of sail.
the-air-ship-boys-or-the-quest-of-the-az: H. L. Sayler's young aeronauts fly south in their airship seeking the lost treasure of the Aztecs. Ruins, jungles, and rivals await in this high-flying adventure. Written when airships promised the future, it captures all the romance of early aviation.
the-bobbsey-twins-at-the-seashore: Laura Lee Hope takes the Bobbseys to the seashore for sand, surf, and a seaside mystery. Nan, Bert, Freddie, and Flossie enjoy classic summer fun in this sunny series entry. Generations of children spent happy hours with the twins by the sea.
alice-sit-by-the-fire: J. M. Barrie's tender comedy follows Alice — a mother returning to children who barely remember her — through misunderstandings toward a loving reconciliation. The creator of Peter Pan shows his gentler, wistful side. A play of great charm and deep feeling.
the-city-of-fire: Grace Livingston Hill — the beloved author of inspirational romances — sets this story against a city of fire, where faith is tested and love refined. Her wholesome fiction comforted millions of readers in troubled times. Romance with a Christian heart, warmly told.
a-study-in-tinguian-folk-lore: Fay-Cooper Cole's pioneering study records the folklore of the Tinguian people of the Philippines — their myths, rituals, and traditions gathered in the field. Early anthropology at its most dedicated and respectful. A precious record of a rich and distinctive culture.
along-the-shore: Rose Hawthorne Lathrop, Nathaniel's gifted daughter, gathers poems of the shore — sea moods, white sails, and the music of waves against rock. Her gentle lyrics carry a painter's eye for light on water and a daughter's inheritance of deep feeling. Quiet, graceful verse from a true minor poet.
lectures-on-dramatic-art-and-literature: August Wilhelm von Schlegel's famous lectures shaped Romantic ideas of drama — Shakespeare, Calderón, and the spirit of the theater. Coleridge and all England learned from them. The founding text of modern dramatic criticism. From Greek tragedy to Shakespeare's stage, his insights lit the way for generations of critics.
a-history-of-english-literature: Robert Huntington Fletcher's history carries students from Beowulf to the moderns — Chaucer, Shakespeare, Milton, and all the great names. Clear, sound, and well-planned, it served generations of classrooms. A reliable guide to England's literary glory. His steady survey leads from Anglo-Saxon songs to the great Victorians with sure judgment.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: Before the Curfew collects Holmes' evening poems — quiet reflections on age, memory, and the coming night. The old poet's wisdom glows gently through these autumnal verses. A beautiful sunset volume from a beloved voice. Twilight thoughts, gently borne, close the day in peace.
dorothy-dainty-at-glenmore: Amy Brooks' Dorothy Dainty goes to Glenmore — new friends, new fun, and gentle lessons for the sweet little heroine. The series' old-fashioned charm continues undimmed. A favorite with young girls for generations, wholesome and kind. Her kind heart wins friends wherever the dainty miss goes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acre: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Acre — St. Jean d'Acre, the last crusader stronghold in the Holy Land. Anthony Maas tells of sieges, kings, and its fall in 1291. Templars and Hospitallers held its walls to the end. The crusades' final chapter was written here.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-in-early: A 1913 entry on Adam in early Christian liturgy and literature — the first man in prayer and legend. Henri Leclercq gathers texts and rites. Lamentations for Adam echo through Lent. The protoplast in the Church's memory.
